refuted.title: SQLite node Database Path becomes expression/data-driven, allowing arbitrary file paths
refuted.evidence:
displayName: 'Database Path',
				name: 'db_path',
				type: 'string',
				default: '',
				placeholder: '/path/to/database.sqlite',
refuted.description:
This diff removes `noDataExpression: true` from the `db_path` parameter. In n8n that flag is what forces a parameter to be a design-time constant; without it the field accepts expressions such as `={{ $json.db_path }}`, so the value is resolved per item from the incoming workflow data at execution time (`this.getNodeParameter('db_path', itemIndex, '')`, line 193).

The resolved value flows unvalidated into two filesystem sinks in `execute()`:
- `const dir = path.dirname(dbPath); ... fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` (lines 208-211) — creates arbitrary directory trees anywhere the n8n process can write.
- `const db = new Database(dbPath, bindings)` (line 224) — opens, and if absent creates, an arbitrary file on the n8n host; a `SELECT` query then returns its contents as node output.

There is no normalisation, no traversal check, and no confinement to a base directory. Because the path is now item-derived, a workflow that binds the field to incoming data (which is the only reason to allow expressions here) lets whoever supplies that data choose which SQLite file the node opens — for example `/home/node/.n8n/database.sqlite`, the n8n instance database containing other workflows and encrypted credentials, or any other readable SQLite file, and it also allows writing new files/directories at attacker-chosen locations.

Note also that `additionalOptions.use_custom_bindings` (line 178) is likewise expression-capable and is passed as `nativeBinding` to better-sqlite3 (line 68), i.e. loads an arbitrary native library. That is pre-existing and untouched here, but it becomes part of the same runtime-data-controlled surface.
refuted.exploit_scenario: An n8n workflow uses a Webhook (or IMAP/HTTP poll) trigger feeding a SQLite Node whose Database Path is now set to an expression over item data, e.g. `={{ $json.database }}` — a configuration this change is specifically enabling. An unauthenticated caller POSTs `{"database": "/home/node/.n8n/database.sqlite"}` to the webhook URL with a query such as `SELECT * FROM credentials_entity`, and the node opens n8n's own database and returns its rows to the workflow output (and to the webhook response, if the workflow responds with the last node). The same input with a path like `/home/node/.n8n/nodes/x/y.sqlite` instead causes arbitrary directory creation and file writes on the host.
refuted.recommendation: Either restore `noDataExpression: true` on `db_path`, or, if data-driven paths are genuinely required, confine the resolved value before use: resolve it with `path.resolve()` against a configured base directory, reject the result if it does not start with that base (`resolvedPath.startsWith(baseDir + path.sep)`), reject paths that are not `.sqlite`/`.db`, and do not create directories outside the base. The same treatment should be applied to `use_custom_bindings`, which should be restricted to a fixed set of known binding paths rather than an arbitrary runtime-supplied native library.

verification.reason: 3/3 verifier(s) agreed — The whole change is the deletion of one UI flag, `noDataExpression: true`, on the `db_path` property (nodes/SqliteNode/v1/SqliteV1.node.ts:111-118); no code in `execute()` changed. `noDataExpression` is an n8n editor-side hint that hides the expression editor for a field — it is not an authorization or path-confinement control, and the value it guards is supplied by the workflow author, who is inside n8n's trust boundary. That author could already type the literal string `/home/node/.n8n/database.sqlite` into the same field with the flag present, and already had expression-capable `query`, `args` and `use_custom_bindings` (line 178, feeding `nativeBinding` at line 68 — arbitrary native library load, i.e. RCE) on the very same node, so the removal grants no capability that did not already exist. The claimed unauthenticated webhook path requires the author to deliberately bind the path to `$json`, which is author misconfiguration of a trusted-by-design field, not a defect introduced by this diff. Searched: I looked for anything that would make `db_path` a security-relevant boundary rather than trusted author config: (1) the full diff (`get_diff`) — the only change in the entire MR is the one-line removal of `noDataExpression`, nothing in `execute()` (lines 190-235) was touched, so no normalisation/confinement was deleted; (2) the repository tree (`list_directory` at root and under nodes/SqliteNode, depth 4) — the repo contains exactly one tracked file, so there is no allowlist, base-directory config, credential, or wrapper elsewhere that either enforces or is meant to enforce path confinement, and there is no caller/host code to inspect; (3) git_log shows only "baseline" and "add feature" commits, so `noDataExpression` was not added as a deliberate hardening measure that is now being reverted. I expected to find, and did not find, any privilege boundary between the person who sets `db_path` and the person who can already set `query`/`args`/`use_custom_bindings` on the same node — all are the same workflow-author-supplied design-time fields, and `use_custom_bindings` (line 178 -> line 68 `nativeBinding`) already grants strictly greater capability (arbitrary native module load) without this change.

That author could already type the literal string `/home/node/.n8n/database.sqlite` into the same field with the flag present, and already had expression-capable `query`, `args` and `use_custom_bindings` (line 178, feeding `nativeBinding` at line 68 — arbitrary native library load, i.e. RCE) on the very same node, so the removal grants no capability that did not already exist. The claimed unauthenticated webhook path requires the author to deliberately bind the path to `$json`, which is author misconfiguration of a trusted-by-design field, not a defect introduced by this diff.

The diff's only change is deleting the UI hint `noDataExpression: true` from the `db_path` property (nodes/SqliteNode/v1/SqliteV1.node.ts:111-118). In n8n `noDataExpression` suppresses the expression toggle in the editor; expression resolution in `getNodeParameter` is unconditional, so a workflow JSON with `={{...}}` in `db_path` was already resolved at runtime before this change — it is an authoring affordance, not a runtime guard. More decisively, the sibling `query` (line 128) and `args` (line 141) parameters were already expression-capable and untouched by this diff, and `query` reaches `db.exec(query)` (line 100, taken for the AUTO/CREATE branch at line 240), so any operator who binds item data into this node already grants arbitrary SQL including `ATTACH DATABASE '/home/node/.n8n/database.sqlite'` and `VACUUM INTO '<path>'` — strictly more power than choosing the db file. The only party who can make `db_path` item-derived is the workflow author, who could already hardcode `/home/node/.n8n/database.sqlite` as a constant; the change therefore grants no capability to any new principal.

The only change in the MR is deleting `noDataExpression: true` from the `db_path` property (nodes/SqliteNode/v1/SqliteV1.node.ts:111-118). `noDataExpression` is an n8n editor flag that disallows the expression editor on a field; it does not restrict *which* paths are accepted. Both before and after this change the field is a free-text `type: 'string'` that a workflow author can set to any absolute path (e.g. `/home/node/.n8n/database.sqlite`), and `execute()` at lines 208-224 never normalised or confined it, so the "arbitrary file path" capability the title claims is introduced is entirely pre-existing and untouched. The only delta is that the value may now be chosen at run time *if* the trusted workflow author deliberately writes an expression binding it to item data — the same posture that already applies to this node's `query`, `args` and `additionalOptions.use_custom_bindings` (the last one passes an arbitrary path as `nativeBinding` to better-sqlite3 at line 68, i.e. loading a native library, and never had the flag), and to n8n's own filesystem nodes. There is no attacker-controlled source that reaches the sink without a trusted operator explicitly wiring it.
